messages:
emma (docs): heads-up — after the mkdocs -> docusaurus migration I’m seeing a number of internal links that only work when the path case matches exactly (e.g. /API/Generate vs /api/generate). broken in prod preview and failing linkcheck in CI. Can we coordinate a small fix?

aj (devex): :eyes: can you paste an example that fails here? is this anchor casing or path casing?

emma (docs): path casing mostly, but some generated anchors changed case too. example from the generate guide: `/guides/Integrations/API#Generate` links to `/guides/integrations/api#generate` on the new site and 404s in the published graph. small repro: `curl -I https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/integrations/API#Generate` returns 404.

noah (eng): CI linkcheck output? that’ll tell us whether it’s the resolver or our nginx redirect rules.

ci-bot: linkcheck: ERROR: broken link found at /guides/Integrations/API (target /guides/integrations/api#generate) — 404. build failed at step docs/linkcheck.

emma (docs): exact CI failure above. I tried adding a temporary redirect rule but didn’t want to ship lots of redirects if we can normalize.

aj (devex): two options: 1) normalize generated slugs to lowercase during build (mkdocs plugin or docusaurus slugify config) 2) add rewrite rules at CDN/nginx to do case-insensitive path resolution for docs routes.

noah (eng): prefer build-time normalization to avoid relying on webserver hacks. downside: it changes canonical URLs (might break external links). we could preserve old casing by emitting redirects for only the handful of mismatches we detect.

lila (i18n): note: changing generated slugs may affect translated page paths. we need to run a quick scan across locales before mass-normalizing.

emma (docs): agreed. my plan: run a detection pass to enumerate mismatches, open a PR that:  - normalizes slugs to lowercase in the docs build pipeline (opt-in in mkdocs.yml)  - emits a generated redirects.json mapping old -> new for the handful of differences  - adds a short migration note for external link owners

aj (devex): happy to land the mkdocs patch. rough mkdocs.yml snippet I tested locally: ```yaml
plugins:
  - slugify:
      lowercase: true
  - linkcheck
```

noah (eng): for docusaurus we can set `slug` in the frontmatter or use the `remark-slug` options. if you want, I’ll add a small script that scans `site_dir` post-build and emits redirects.json.

emma (docs): that would be great. I forked a tiny script that greps for Title -> generated slug collisions: ```bash
# find headings that would produce uppercase slugs
grep -R "^#" docs/ | sed -E "s/:.*$//" | while read f; do
  # simulate slugify (lowercased would differ)
  title=$(head -n1 "$f")
  slug=$(echo "$title" | tr -cd '[:alnum:] ' | tr ' ' '-')
  if echo "$slug" | grep '[A-Z]'; then echo "$f -> $slug"; fi
done
```

ci-bot: preview build: staging preview available at https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/pr-1234 — linkcheck still failing on that preview for a couple old links.

emma (docs): PR (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1234 — contains the mkdocs plugin toggle and the redirects generator. Please review: aj for config, noah for the redirect script, lila for i18n impact.

aj (devex): will review tonight and try the toggle on a full build. if it’s clean we can ship the slug normalization behind a feature flag and enable redirects for legacy paths only. :thumbsup:

noah (eng): I’ll add the small post-build redirect generator and push a patch to the PR tomorrow morning.

lila (i18n): I’ll run the script against the `i18n/` tree and send a short list of pages that would change. we might need to keep a few legacy slugs for language-specific reasons.

emma (docs): thanks all — goal: avoid large-scale redirects but make the site linkcheck-green and preserve external links where we can. tagging follow-ups: @aj, @noah, @lila.

aj (devex): noted. I’ll post status in this thread when I’ve run a full mkdocs build on the branch.

emma (docs): perfect — if anyone finds other broken anchor/casing patterns ping me and I’ll add them to PR checklist. :sparkles:
